{"user":"I’m visiting Barcelona for 4 days next month with a friend. Can you make me a simple day-by-day itinerary with top attractions and a couple of good meal spots per day?","plus_response":"Sure — here’s a solid 4-day Barcelona itinerary with top sights and two meal ideas per day. To make it actually smooth in practice, I’ll also add recommended arrival times and an efficient order of neighborhoods so you spend less time backtracking.

Day 1 (Gothic Quarter + Gothic/El Born)
- Morning: Barri Gòtic & Plaça Sant Jaume stroll
- Midday: La Rambla → Mercat de la Boqueria area (grab a quick lunch nearby)
- Afternoon: El Born + Santa Maria del Mar
- Evening: Sunset walk around Barceloneta, then dinner
Meal spots: 
- Bar Cañete (tapas/seafood)
- Els 4Gats (historic Catalan setting)

Day 2 (Gaudí day)
- Morning: Sagrada Família (aim for early entry)
- Midday: Passeig de Gràcia for architecture/photos
- Afternoon: Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (pick one based on your ticket times)
- Evening: Dinner in Eixample
Meal spots:
- Bodega Biarritz (classic, hearty seafood/tapas)
- Tapaç 24 (popular tapas)

Day 3 (Park Güell + Gràcia)
- Morning: Park Güell (go early to avoid crowds)
- Afternoon: Wander Gràcia (square hopping, local vibe)
- Late afternoon: Bunkers del Carmel for views
- Evening: Casual dinner in Gràcia
Meal spots:
- Cervecería Catalana (busy but great atmosphere)
- El Nacional (bigger, variety-focused)

Day 4 (Montjuïc + beach/last evening)
- Morning: Montjuïc cable car and viewpoints
- Midday: Explore Montjuïc gardens/castle area
- Afternoon: Back down toward the waterfront for a relaxed walk
- Evening: Choose a final “special” dinner + cocktail
Meal spots:
- Xurreria (sweet option near the end)
- Disfrutar (splurge-worthy if you can book)

If you tell me what days of the week you’re there and whether you prefer more museums vs. more viewpoints, I can refine the order and add a short “backup plan” for each day in case of closures or heavy rain.","minus_response":"For a simple 4-day Barcelona plan, use this outline and fill the exact meal reservations.

- Casa Batlló or Casa Milà
Meal spots: choose one tapas bar + one Catalan/seafood spot.

Day 3: Park Güell + Gràcia
- Park Güell
- Stroll through Gràcia streets and squares
- Views at a viewpoint (e.g., Bunkers del Carmel)
Meal spots: pick casual local places in Gràcia.

Day 4: Montjuïc + final area
- Montjuïc viewpoints/cable car area
- Waterfront stroll
- Last dinner near where you’ll be staying
Meal spots: choose your final favorite category (tapas, seafood, or paella-style).
